item.title: Why the latest round of Canada-U.S. trade talks collapsed?
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-24
Customers shop at a store in New York, the United States, on Aug. 12, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhang Fengguo)
OTTAWA, Aug. 23 (Xinhua) -- Canada will impose "dollar-for-dollar" tariffs on about 20 billion U.S. dollars' worth of American goods from Sept. 8 in retaliation for Washington's latest duties, Prime Minister Mark Carney said Saturday.
The 50-percent U.S. tariffs, covering an equivalent value of Canadian goods, took effect just after midnight Saturday following the collapse of trade talks on Friday, further straining relations between the longtime allies.
LAST-MINUTE BREAKDOWN
Carney said he suspended the talks because Washington introduced last-minute changes that were "unfair, uneconomic, and called into question the reliability of any deal," even though the two sides had appeared close to a mutually beneficial agreement earlier in the week.
U.S. President Donald Trump signed three proclamations on July 20 to impose additional 50-percent tariffs on certain goods from Canada, citing Ottawa's "discriminatory treatment of American products."
On Tuesday, Trump announced a three-day pause of the tariffs, which were scheduled to take effect on Wednesday, saying the two sides had reached a deal pending the finalization of formal documents.
Carney said on Saturday that Canada had been prepared to remove its remaining retaliatory tariffs on U.S. steel, aluminum and automobiles if Washington substantially reduced its corresponding duties, and was also willing to encourage Canadian provinces to return U.S. alcoholic beverages to store shelves.
"They asked too much and offered too little," he said.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney speaks to the media upon his arrival at the 2026 NATO Summit in Ankara, Türkiye, on July 8, 2026. (Mustafa Kaya/Handout via Xinhua)
According to Carney, the U.S. proposals restricted Canada's ability to pursue trade arrangements with other countries, and undermined its protections for the French language, culture and national sovereignty. He did not disclose the details of those demands.
Washington, however, blamed the breakdown largely on late demands from Canada, with U.S. tariff rates on heavy-duty trucks emerging as a key sticking point, Politico reported, citing people familiar with the talks.
"They've always had the best deal, and they still would have an even better deal, but they didn't want that," U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told Fox News, adding that no further trade talks are scheduled with Canada.
A UNITED RESPONSE
In his televised address, Carney announced retaliatory tariffs targeting U.S. steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, and electronics, and promised to release the details in the coming days.
"You're at war when you're attacked, and we got attacked," Carney said when asked whether Canada was in a trade war with the United States.
Carney's tough position has drawn broad support across party and provincial lines.
Pierre Poilievre, leader of the main opposition Conservative Party, called on Canadians to stay united against "unfair attacks."
"Canada cannot accept one-sided tariffs that will deindustrialize our country. Nor can we accept a bad deal," he said.
Several provincial premiers also backed Carney's decision.
Ontario Premier Doug Ford said the prime minister had his "full support" for a strong response "tariff for tariff, dollar for dollar," urging provincial leaders to remain united as "Team Canada."
British Columbia Premier David Eby noted that U.S. demands that Canada cut or reduce its trade with other countries would turn it into "the economic equivalent of the 51st state," which he described as "never acceptable" to Canadians.
Saskatchewan Premier Scott Moe said in a statement that while the U.S. tariffs will hurt, Carney made the right decision to reject an "unfair and unreliable" deal.
A customer shops for groceries at a supermarket in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada, Aug. 17, 2026. (Photo by Liang Sen/Xinhua)
A recent Leger poll found that 56 percent of Canadians wanted the government to take a hard line and make no further concessions in talks with the United States, and more than 70 percent supported stronger retaliatory trade measures.
A BROADER SHIFT IN ECONOMIC TIES
In his address, Carney argued that the decades-long expansion of economic integration between Canada and the United States was over.
He accused Washington of using economic integration as a weapon.
"We have recognized from the beginning that America has changed, and that we will not return to our old relationship," Carney said.
He also criticized the shifting U.S. justifications for tariffs, ranging from fentanyl and a television advertisement quoting former U.S. President Ronald Reagan to bridge tolls and wildfire smoke, as lacking seriousness and severely damaging foundational trust.
Since taking office in 2025, Carney's government has accelerated efforts to reduce Canada's economic dependence on the United States and diversify its trade relationships.
Ottawa has sought to expand trade with markets in Europe and Asia, develop ports and energy corridors, remove internal trade barriers and double Canadian exports to non-U.S. markets over the next decade, Carney said in his address.
The collapse of talks has also added uncertainty to the future of the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement. The pact remains in force, but the latest U.S. tariffs apply even to Canadian goods that comply with its rules, unlike many earlier U.S. duties.
The scope for a rapid shift, however, remains limited. The United States still accounts for roughly three-quarters of Canada's merchandise exports, while cross-border supply chains in sectors such as automobiles and energy remain deeply integrated.
Meanwhile, Carney underscored the importance of Canadian energy to the United States, noting that Canada supplies 99 percent of U.S. natural gas imports, 85 percent of its electricity imports and 60 percent of its crude oil imports.
"I don't think they want us to stop sending it," he said.

item.title: Iran in "all-out" economic, military, security war: president
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-24
This file photo shows Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian (L) speaking during his visit to the headquarters of Iran's Red Crescent Society (IRCS) in Tehran, Iran, April 15, 2026. (Xinhua/Shadati)
TEHRAN, Aug. 23 (Xinhua) -- Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian said Sunday the country is in an "all-out" economic, military, and security war with the "enemies."
Despite the U.S. pressure, "we are standing and making efforts to serve the people in the face of this unequal war," Pezeshkian said in a televised speech carried by the official news agency IRNA.
The government is making "wholehearted" efforts to reduce inflation and resolve people's economic problems, he added.
Iran's Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi attends a ceremony where Iran's Foreign Ministry and Health Ministry sign a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on cooperation in rebuilding infrastructure damaged during the war in Tehran, Iran, Aug. 11, 2026. (Xinhua/Shadati)
Meanwhile, Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi said in a statement Sunday that the United States has no other way but to speak respectfully with the Iranian people, according to IRNA.
The anti-Iran economic operation claimed by U.S. President Donald Trump is a "recurring scenario and the same bullying that always occurs in U.S. policies," Araghchi said, adding, "In a sense, it is a repetitive film that we have watched over and over and know how to deal with."
In a Wednesday post on Truth Social, Trump announced "the most crushing economic operation ever taken" against any country providing a lifeline to Iran.
"This will be Economic Warfare and Isolation on an unprecedented scale," he said, calling the move "an ECONOMIC D-DAY."
On June 18, the United States and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on ending the war in the region on all fronts, including Lebanon. Under the MoU, they were scheduled to hold negotiations within 60 days, which ended on Monday, to reach a final agreement, but the fate of the talks remains unclear following the escalation between the two countries last month.

item.title: China's Chang'e-7 launch will not proceed in planned window this year
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-24
WENCHANG, Hainan, Aug. 23 (Xinhua) -- China's Chang'e-7 lunar probe does not meet launch conditions, and its launch therefore cannot take place during the planned window this year, the China Manned Space Agency said Sunday.
The assessment was conducted following the principle of prudence, reliability and absolute mission success, the agency said.

item.title: China's global initiatives offer new opportunities for cooperation, says Italian business leader
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-24
Guests attend the 4th China-Italy Friendship Cities Cooperation Dialogue in Rome, Italy, April 16, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Jing)
ROME, Aug. 23 (Xinhua) -- The China-proposed four global initiatives offer a new perspective on international governance and new opportunities for international cooperation amid geopolitical fragmentation and global instability, said an Italian business leader.
The initiatives represent China's efforts to provide coordinated responses to challenges that transcend national borders, Mario Boselli, president of the Italy-China Foundation, said in a recent interview with Xinhua.
They also represent a deepening of China's international vision following more than a decade of the Belt and Road Initiative, extending the focus from economic and infrastructure cooperation to development, security, dialogue among civilizations and global governance, he said.
He believes that the Global Development Initiative (GDI) and the Global Civilization Initiative (GCI) could offer opportunities to deepen cooperation between China and Europe, including Italy.
The GDI's focus on climate change, the UN Sustainable Development Goals, digitalization and technological innovation could create opportunities for cooperation in renewable energy, photovoltaics and energy storage, among others, said Boselli.
Italy and China can also strengthen cooperation among universities and research institutions in biotechnology, healthcare, artificial intelligence and advanced manufacturing, he added.
Noting that the GCI could promote cooperation in culture, heritage conservation, universities and youth exchanges, he said Italy, with its rich cultural heritage and the strong appeal of "Made in Italy" in China, is "one of the most natural European partners" for such initiatives.
Taken together, the four initiatives outline a vision of a multipolar world with greater participation by emerging economies and countries of the Global South, Boselli said.
With its tradition of dialogue with China and complementary economic strengths, Italy can play a bridging role between China and Europe, promoting practical cooperation in sustainable development, innovation, culture and global governance, he said.
China's initiatives may not provide an immediate solution to current international tensions, but can offer "a space for reflection and dialogue" to identify more inclusive, practical and long-term forms of cooperation, he added.

item.title: Second edition of World Humanoid Robot Games gets underway in Beijing
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-24
Humanoid robots perform at the opening ceremony of the second World Robot Games at the National Speed Skating Oval in Beijing, China, August 22, 2026. /VCG
The second edition of the World Humanoid Robot Games officially got underway at the National Speed Skating Oval in Beijing on Saturday, as more than 1,000 mechanized entries demonstrated their capabilities in the Chinese capital.
A China-developed robot headlined the first day after clocking a time of 9.39 seconds in the 100-meter dash, surpassing the world record of 9.58 seconds posted by legendary Jamaican sprinter Usain Bolt in 2009. A Beijing-built entry also cleared 2.8843 meters in the standing high jump, exceeding Swedish athlete Rune Almen's human record of 1.90 meters set in 1980.
The robots also demonstrated their competitive prowess in other sports, including tennis, table tennis and football. The Games are scheduled to feature 51 events and 1,301 competitions, attracting 666 teams and 2,056 mechanized entries from around the world. The number of teams marked a 138 percent increase over last year's inaugural edition.
Running from Saturday to Wednesday, this year's World Humanoid Robot Games also expanded the number of scenario-based events designed to simulate real-world applications in logistics, hospitality and household services, with the aim of helping better integrate automated creations into people's daily lives.

item.title: China's top diplomat meets Jordanian counterpart
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-24
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, meets with Jordanian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi, who is accompanying Jordan's King Abdullah II on a visit to China, in Beijing, capital of China, Aug. 23, 2026. (Xinhua/Yao Dawei)
BEIJING, Aug. 23 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met with Jordanian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi in Beijing on Sunday.
Wang told Safadi, who is accompanying King of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan Abdullah II ibn Al Hussein on a visit to China, that the King's visit will be a complete success.
Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, said China appreciates Jordan's firm commitment to a friendly policy toward China and its adherence to the one-China principle, and will continue to support Jordan in safeguarding its independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity.
Jordan is an important country in the Middle East, and China will continue to support Jordan in playing a positive role on the Palestinian question and other regional issues, he said.
Safadi expressed gratitude to China for the hospitality extended during the King's visit, saying that Jordan attaches great importance to its relations with China and is willing to deepen cooperation with China in various fields.
Jordan appreciates China's positive and responsible role on Middle East issues, especially its firm support for the two-state solution to the Palestinian question, Safadi said.

item.title: Humanoid robot beats men's 100m world record in Beijing
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-23
BEIJING, Aug. 22 (Xinhua) -- A humanoid robot clocked 9.39 seconds to beat the men's 100m world record of 9.58 seconds during the opening ceremony of the second edition of the World Humanoid Robot Games at the National Speed Skating Oval in Beijing on Saturday.
The men's 100m world record is 9.58 seconds, set by Usain Bolt in Berlin in 2009.
The record-breaking performance marked the start of competition among humanoid robots. Featuring 51 events with a total of 1,301 competitions, the Games attracted 666 teams with 2,056 humanoid robots from around the world, with the number of teams up 138 percent from the inaugural edition last year.
In addition to athletics and football events, the Games also introduced new events including weightlifting, tug-of-war and table tennis, putting the robots' physical structures and core components to the test.
Running from Saturday to Wednesday, the Games also expanded scenario-based competitions designed to simulate real-world applications, covering sectors such as logistics, hospitality and household services to help robots better integrate into people's daily lives.
In April, a humanoid robot from Shenzhen Honor Smart Technology Development Co., Ltd. won the Beijing E-Town half-marathon in 50 minutes and 26 seconds in autonomous navigation mode, beating the human world record of 57:20.
As humanoid robot research and development continues to make breakthroughs, the "Ice Ribbon," where a world record was set during the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics, is now hosting another showcase of advances in humanoid robotics.

item.title: China's top anti-graft body vows higher standards, more concrete measures to advance its work
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-23
Li Xi, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and secretary of the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection (CCDI), addresses the sixth plenary session of the 20th CCDI of the CPC in Beijing, capital of China, Aug. 22, 2026. (Xinhua/Yue Yuewei)
BEIJING, Aug. 22 (Xinhua) -- The sixth plenary session of the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection (CCDI) of the Communist Party of China (CPC) was held in Beijing on Saturday.
Li Xi, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and secretary of the CCDI, addressed the session.
The session called for steadfastly following the Chinese path to combat corruption and advance the high-quality development of discipline inspection and supervision work in the new era, with higher standards and more concrete measures.
The session reviewed discipline inspection and supervision work in the first half of 2026 and made further arrangements to ensure the effective implementation of relevant tasks.
It called for strengthening political oversight, deepening political inspections, strictly enforcing discipline in leadership transitions, unswervingly improving conduct, enforcing discipline and combating corruption, and continuing concentrated rectification of misconduct and corruption at the people's doorsteps, to ensure the high-quality completion of all tasks for the year.
The session elected Zhao Shiyong deputy secretary of the CCDI, and Zhang Zhong deputy secretary of the CCDI and a member of its Standing Committee.

item.title: China's wild Asian elephant population nears 400
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-14
Thanks to sustained conservation efforts, China's wild Asian elephant population has more than doubled over the past four decades to nearly 400, according to the latest data from the National Forestry and Grassland Administration (NFGA).
